missions.name: First Light at Shackleton
missions.location: Rim of Shackleton crater, lunar south pole

illumination.label: Full sunlight on the crater rim

briefing.tagline: Your first command: keep a crew of 4 alive for 12 days at the lunar south pole.
briefing.story: The lander touched down on the sunlit rim of Shackleton crater. Near the pole the Sun never climbs high: it circles the horizon, so solar panels get light for long stretches — until a hill or crater rim casts a shadow over the base. Everything your crew needs to survive came with you on the lander, and the lander could only carry so much.
objectives: Keep oxygen, water and food above zero for 12 days
Keep the base powered — life support cannot switch off
Keep the crew's radiation dose below 250 mSv
hazards: A solar storm is forecast for day 5
Days 8–10: the base falls into terrain shadow — very little solar power
Random equipment failures, dust and leaks
briefing.tip: Every kilogram counts. Batteries carry you through the shadow; a shelter protects you from the storm — can you afford both?

missions.name: Artemis Base Camp
missions.location: Connecting ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters

illumination.label: Sun sinking behind the crater rim

briefing.tagline: 28 days. Not enough room on the lander to bring everything — you will have to make it.
briefing.story: This is a longer stay. The habitat's storage room can't hold four weeks of water, oxygen and food. To last, the base has to recycle water, split water into oxygen and grow some of its own food — and every one of those machines needs power, even when the Sun disappears behind the crater rim.
objectives: Survive 28 days with a crew of 4
Close the loop: recycle and produce what storage can't hold
Keep the crew's radiation dose below 250 mSv
hazards: Two solar storms: day 10 (moderate) and day 22 (severe)
Two shadow periods — the second one is very dark
Random equipment failures, dust, leaks and crop disease
briefing.tip: Storage limits mean open-loop supplies alone won't last. Check the projected days of autonomy before you launch.
